# UI night run — durable state

The presentation half of the project. This file is to the `ui-polish` branch
what `NIGHT_RUN.md` is to `main`: the memory that survives a summarised context.

**Do not edit `NIGHT_RUN.md` from this branch, and do not edit this file from
`main`.** Two streams writing the same log is the one guaranteed merge conflict,
and it is entirely avoidable.

## The two streams

| | `main` | `ui-polish` |
|---|---|---|
| What | rules, scoring, structures, parameters | how it looks and feels |
| Who | live conversation with the user | this hourly run |
| Owns | `src/*.ts`, `src/lens/**`, `src/hex/**`, `tools/**`, `src/__tests__/**` | `src/components/**`, `src/index.css`, `src/App.tsx` |

`src/useRun.ts` is logic and belongs to `main`. `src/App.tsx` is layout and
belongs here. They were one 597-line file until the split that preceded this
run, which is what makes the two streams separable at all.

### Every firing

    git fetch origin
    git reset --hard origin/ui-polish     # the fired branch carries no work
    git merge origin/main                 # take the night's rules work
    npm install                           # only if node_modules is missing
    ... one backlog item ...
    npm test && npx tsc -b --noEmit && npm run smoke
    git push origin HEAD:ui-polish

Merging `main` **into** this branch every hour is the whole trick: the branches
never diverge by more than one firing, so the morning merge back into `main` is
nearly a fast-forward instead of one painful reconciliation. No rebase, no force
push, no rewritten history.

**If that merge conflicts, stop and report it.** Do not resolve it. A confident
wrong resolution in shared code breaks the game silently, and this is the one
thing worth waking the user for.

## Standing rules

- **Never touch the files `main` owns.** If a polish item seems to need a change
  to scoring, geometry or config, it is the wrong item — note it here and pick
  the next one. Half of this run's value is that it cannot break the rules.
- **Never run `npm run probe`.** It rewrites `src/metrics.generated.ts`, which
  belongs to `main`, and would conflict every single hour.
- **Three DOM attributes are a contract with the logic layer**: `data-cell`,
  `data-hex` and `data-hand-index`. Dragging finds the cell under the pointer by
  the first two; the discard animation freezes cards by the third. Renaming any
  of them breaks input with nothing failing to warn you. They may be added to,
  never renamed or removed.
- `npm run smoke` must pass before pushing. It drives the built app through
  place, drag, undo, discard, reseed, hex, lock-and-cash and all three screens.
  It is the only check that catches presentation changes that break interaction.
- One item per firing, finished. A half-landed animation is worse than none.

## The visual budget

Unattended taste is the real risk here, so these are hard limits rather than
preferences. An animation that breaks one of them is wrong even if it looks
good.

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| No animation over **250ms** | Anything longer sits between the player and their next decision. |
| Nothing may delay input | Animations decorate a state change that has already happened; they never gate it. |
| Every animation honours `prefers-reduced-motion` | Already wired in `index.css`. Extend it, never bypass it. |
| No new dependency | Everything here is CSS and React. A motion library is a decision for the user, not for 3am. |
| Never cover the board | The bug that started this backlog was a panel covering the cell being aimed at. |
| Time-to-first-placement must not grow | Measured by the smoke test. Polish that slows the opening is a regression. |

Colour stays inside the existing language: sky = chips, amber = mult, emerald =
score, violet/pink = full lines, grey = sealed. Adding a hue means inventing a
meaning, and there isn't one spare.

## Queue

Ordered so a short night still lands the items that change how a placement
*feels*. One per firing.

- [x] **1. Score-fly and count-up.** The banked score flies from the placed cell
      to the score display, which counts up rather than snapping to the new
      total. The single highest-value item here: it is what makes a placement
      feel like it paid. Reuse the discard fly-away's approach — freeze a
      position, animate, never gate the state change.
- [x] **2. Weighted drag.** The card tilts into its direction of travel and
      settles with a slight overshoot; cells lift a little under the pointer.
      Small, and it is most of what "physicality" means. `useCardDrag` already
      tracks position — velocity is a derivative of what is there.
- [x] **3. Run end.** Winning and losing are currently a status string. Give the
      run a proper end: final score against target, the best placement of the
      run (it is in the log), and a button to replay the same seed. The biggest
      hole in the current UI.
- [ ] **4. Line-scoring cascade.** When a placement scores, light the
      contributing cells one at a time rather than all at once, chips axis then
      mult axis. Makes the row/column split legible as motion instead of colour.
- [ ] **5. Line-complete punctuation.** A run reaching the cap currently gets a
      static marker. Give it a beat: a snap, a brief glow, and the marker
      arriving rather than appearing.
- [ ] **6. Near-miss feedback.** An illegal drop is silently refused. Show why
      for a moment — would exceed the cap, sealed, not touching anything.
- [ ] **7. Card faces.** Proper pips, a clearer rank/suit hierarchy, subtle
      stock texture. Functional but plain today.
- [ ] **8. Board depth.** Stronger well shading, a felt or paper ground, a
      warmer highlight on legal cells.
- [ ] **9. Hand tray.** Fan the cards slightly, lift on hover, and animate the
      refill as a deal rather than a pop-in.

## Where things live

- **Artifact (this branch)**: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/55baefb7-5439-4a2e-b45b-236ca617ff05
  Title "Grid Poker — UI polish", favicon ✨ — keep both stable. Always pass
  that address as `url`; omitting it mints a new artifact every firing and the
  user loses the link. It currently holds the *pre-polish baseline*, so the
  first firing's publish is also the first before/after comparison.

  **Never publish to the artifact on `main`**
  (`6613c961-31a5-4a7b-8c61-abeb633d25e6`). That is the build the user plays
  while the rules stream works, and overwriting it from here would replace their
  game with a half-finished polish branch.
- **Build**: `npx vite build`, then inline `dist/assets/*.css` and `*.js` into a
  single body-only HTML file — no doctype, html, head or body tags, the host
  wraps it. Nothing may reference an external host.
- **Browser**: `import { launch } from './tools/browser.mjs'`. Chromium is
  pre-installed; the npm `playwright` package pins a different build than the
  image ships, so an explicit executablePath is required and the helper resolves
  it. Never run `playwright install`. Scripts must live inside the repo or node
  cannot resolve `playwright`.
- **Commit signatures are fine.** Every commit is signed and a SessionStart hook
  configures verification. If one ever reads as missing or bad, the fault is in
  that setup — run `python3 tools/setup-signing.py`. Never rewrite history over
  it; a previous firing lost a whole cycle to exactly that.

## Decisions log

Append here rather than to `NIGHT_RUN.md`. Record anything a later firing would
otherwise have to rediscover, and anything you tried that looked wrong once it
was moving — a note that an idea failed is worth as much as one that landed.

- **Item 1.** `useRun.ts` already exposes everything needed without touching
  it: `logRows` grows by exactly one entry per placement or cash (never on a
  discard, undo, new run or ruleset switch, since those either don't append to
  the log or replace history wholesale), and each row already carries
  `atLabel` in the same `"r,c"` / `"q,r"` format the board writes into
  `data-cell` / `data-hex`. So the fly-source lookup and the trigger condition
  both come from data `main` already produces — no shared file needed a
  change.
- Gave the score number in `StatusBar` a `data-score-display` attribute
  (additive, not a rename, so it doesn't touch the three-attribute contract)
  and had `App.tsx` query it at animation time rather than threading a ref
  down — the same `document.querySelector` pattern the existing discard
  fly-away already uses for hand-index rects, so the two features stay
  consistent.
- `StatusBar` renders twice (docked-mobile header copy, wide-desktop aside
  copy) and only one is visible via a `hidden` class at a time — a
  `display:none` element reports a zero-size `getBoundingClientRect()`, so the
  destination lookup walks all `[data-score-display]` matches and takes the
  first with nonzero width/height rather than assuming a single instance.
- Tried letting the fly-and-count-up run the visual budget's full 250ms and it
  read as sluggish next to the rest of the interaction — landed on 220ms for
  both the CSS fly and the JS count-up tween, driven by the same constant in
  each file (`SCORE_FLY_MS` in `App.tsx`, `COUNT_UP_MS` in `StatusBar.tsx`) so
  they keep landing together if either changes.
- Considered animating the progress bar width with a separate CSS transition
  layered on top of the count-up. Dropped it — the bar's width is already
  bound to the tweened display value, so it moves smoothly for free, and a
  second transition on top of an already-interpolated value just adds a lag
  between the number and the bar rather than any visible improvement.
- The existing `discard-fly` (380ms) and `deal-in` (320ms) animations already
  exceed the 250ms budget — they predate this backlog and are not this item's
  to fix. Left them alone; noting it here so a later firing doesn't assume the
  budget was already being enforced everywhere.
- **Item 2.** `useCardDrag` (`src/useCardDrag.ts`) is a top-level `src/*.ts`
  file, so it belongs to `main` — the queue note that it "already tracks
  position" turned out to matter literally: velocity had to be derived outside
  the hook, from consecutive `drag.x` samples taken in `App.tsx`, rather than
  by adding a field to the hook's state.
- Tilt is computed in a `useEffect` keyed on `drag`: each pointermove gives a
  new `drag` object, so the effect fires once per sample, diffs `drag.x`
  against the previous sample's `{x, t}` (via `performance.now()`), and turns
  `vx` (px/ms) into a lean clamped to ±18° around a −4° resting angle (the
  same static angle the ghost used before this item). Position (`left`/`top`)
  stays a direct, untransitioned read of `drag.x`/`drag.y` so the card never
  lags the pointer — only the rotation inside the ghost's `transform` carries
  a `transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)` (a
  standard "easeOutBack"), which is what gives the lean its spring/overshoot
  instead of snapping to each new sample.
- First attempt tied "settles with a slight overshoot" only to the drop, on
  the theory that release is when a dragged object's motion actually stops.
  It doesn't work: `useCardDrag` nulls `drag` synchronously on pointer-up, so
  the ghost unmounts in the same tick — there is no frame in which a
  post-drop settle animation could ever be seen. Moved the idea to where it
  *is* visible: a pointer that stops moving mid-drag (still held down, no new
  samples) now eases back to the resting −4° via an 80ms idle timer that
  resets the tilt, so the overshoot plays whenever motion decelerates to a
  stop, not only at an invisible drop.
  Verified this distinction by instrumenting the effect with a temporary
  `console.debug` and reading it back over Playwright's `page.on('console')`:
  a fast flick pinned `vx` at the ±18° clamp as expected, and the same probe
  caught the idle timer firing before a screenshot taken \>80ms after the
  last sample — explaining why an early screenshot read as barely tilted
  before the timing was corrected. The debug line was removed before commit;
  noting the method here since a later firing chasing a similar "why is the
  number smaller than I expected" will hit the same idle-window trap.
- The cell lift (a `translateY(-3px)`, plus a stronger drop-shadow on the
  grid board) is applied only to the currently-targeted, selectable cell
  while `dragActive` (a plain `Boolean(drag)` passed down from `App.tsx`),
  not merely on hover — the standing hover highlight already existed and
  this item is specifically about drag physicality, so the lift is additive
  and scoped to the drag case rather than changing the general hover
  behaviour click-selection already relies on.
- Hex cells use `clip-path` to draw the hexagon, which crops any box-shadow
  applied to the element itself — so the grid board's lift got a drop-shadow
  and the hex board's got translateY only. Both stay within the 150ms
  transition already on those cells (extended to include `transform`
  alongside the existing `background-color`/`box-shadow` list).

- **Item 3.** Everything needed already exists without touching a `main`-owned
  file: `state.status` ('playing' | 'won' | 'lost') and `state.score` come
  from `useRun`, `cfg.targetScore` from the ruleset config, `state.seed` is
  already what `handleNewRun` takes (so "replay this seed" is just
  `g.handleNewRun(state.seed)` — no new plumbing), and the best placement is
  `logRows` reduced by `.score`, the same `LogRow` shape `ScoreLog` already
  renders from.
- New `RunEndPanel.tsx` takes over the hand tray's spot once
  `state.status !== 'playing'` rather than laying a panel over the board.
  `HandTray` is already fully non-interactive at that point (its own
  `disabled={!playing}` prop disables selection and discard), so the space
  was dead regardless — reusing it satisfies "never cover the board" without
  a special case, and it worked out to a `trayOrEnd` ternary shared by both
  the docked-mobile footer and the wide-desktop layout, so the panel appears
  in exactly the one place a hand would have been on either layout.
- Left the compact WIN/LOSS strip inside `StatusBar` alone rather than
  folding it into this item. It's a different job — a quiet, always-in-view
  status readout in a panel that's on screen throughout play — while
  `RunEndPanel` is the actionable "what now" screen with the replay CTA.
  Removing the strip would have meant the docked-mobile top bar loses its
  only end-of-run signal while the eye is still up there; keeping both was
  cheaper and safer than restructuring `StatusBar` to make room for a CTA it
  was never laid out for.
- Entrance is a single `run-end-in` keyframe (translateY(10px)+scale(0.97) →
  none) at 200ms, under the 250ms cap, added next to the other keyframes in
  `index.css` — it falls under the file's existing blanket
  `prefers-reduced-motion` rule for free, same as every other animation
  there, so nothing extra was needed to honour it.
- Considered a modal/overlay treatment (centred card, dimmed backdrop) since
  "biggest hole in the current UI" reads like it wants weight. Dropped it:
  a full-screen dim necessarily sits on top of the board, which is exactly
  what the visual budget's "never cover the board" rule exists to prevent,
  regardless of whether the run is still live — the rule doesn't carve out
  an end-of-run exception, and the hand-tray slot gives enough visual weight
  (full-width panel, large score, its own color) without needing to occlude
  anything.
- Verified live in headless Chromium against the build: drove the default
  ruleset with a scripted greedy placement loop (select hand-index 0, click
  the first cell that actually reduces placements-left, so it's robust to
  both adjacency-gated and free-placement rulesets and to the row/line cap
  making some empty cells illegal) until `placementsLeft` hit 0, producing a
  genuine LOSS at 444/610 under the "Free placement" ruleset. Confirmed the
  panel's text, the best-placement chip (correctly picked the run's actual
  highest-scoring entry off the log), and — critically — that "Replay this
  seed" actually starts a fresh run on the same seed (`grid-poker-1`
  visible in the seed box throughout, score back to 0, hand tray back in
  place of the panel). Did not separately chase a live WIN capture: none of
  the presets reachable from the UI (`SetupPage` has no raw target-score
  field, only preset selection) have a target low enough for naive greedy
  play to reliably clear within their placement budget, and the WIN branch
  is the same component on the same data with only a ternary swapping
  text/color/accent — already exercised by `tsc` and visually identical in
  structure to the verified LOSS render. Screenshots (session-local, not
  committed): `runend-01.png` (run-over panel, mid-board), `runend-02-after-replay.png`
  (post-replay, panel gone, hand tray restored, score 0/610).

For each item: what shipped, what it cost in milliseconds, and a screenshot or

  (fly trigger + render), `StatusBar.tsx` (count-up + `data-score-display`)
